title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning and Runbook Standards
author: Ari Chen
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's standards for SRE documentation focused on SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and runbook structure. The goal is to provide a consistent, actionable set of templates and thresholds that teams can adopt for any public-facing and internal inference services.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to eng-sre, eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, and product teams owning customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Audience: SREs, service owners, on-call responders, and engineering managers.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets
- Principle: SLOs must reflect customer-impacting behavior (availability, latency, correctness) and be measurable from production signals.
- Required SLO fields: name, objective, measurement window, signal(s), alerting thresholds, owner, and linked runbook.
- Example SLOs (reference):
  - Generation API availability: 99.95% monthly (measured by successful 2xx responses end-to-end).
  - Chat endpoint p95 latency: < 300ms (request-to-first-byte) over 30d rolling window.
  - Embeddings throughput: 99% of requests finish within configured concurrency limits.
- Error budget policy (standardized):
  - Green: remaining error budget >= 50% — normal ops.
  - Yellow: 20% <= remaining < 50% — no non-essential releases; SRE and owner review weekly.
  - Red: remaining < 20% — freeze risky deploys, schedule immediate reliability initiative within 7 days, increase monitoring cadence.
  - Burn rate escalations: if burn rate > 4x expected within 24h, open an incident and notify platform on-call.
- Measurement guidance: use synthetic traffic, customer-facing telemetry, and internal tracing. Prefer end-to-end checks that include routing/fallback behavior.

2) Capacity planning and runway
- Objectives: ensure headroom for predictable throughput, minimize tail latency due to resource saturation, and avoid unexpected throttling for enterprise customers.
- Forecast cadence: quarterly forecasts with monthly reconciliations. Forecast inputs: recent 90d traffic, sales commitments (Dedicated), upcoming marketing events, model changes that affect token cost.
- Headroom policy: maintain baseline 30% spare serving capacity for hosted API; Dedicated capacity should include smallest committed burst buffer (configurable per contract).
- Runway calculation (example):
  - RequiredCapacity = PeakQPS * AvgTokenPerRequest * SafetyFactor(1.3)
  - Ordering lead times: GPU procurement / cloud reserved capacity timelines documented per region (default 8-12 weeks).
- Scaling playbook:
  1. Monitor: CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, tail latency.
  2. Auto-scale: within Dedicated pools follow autoscaling policies (min/max nodes).
  3. Manual: if projected utilization will exceed 80% sustained for 72h, open capacity request to infra and notify sales for quota changes.

3) Reliability initiatives and investments
- Annual reliability planning: each team must propose at least one reliability initiative per quarter (examples: caching improvements, KV prefix caching for heavy prompt sets, batching optimization).
- Project selection criteria: measurable impact on SLO attainment, cost savings, or operational complexity reduction. Define success metrics and rollout plan.
- Verification: use canaries and A/B rollout; monitor SLO delta against baseline and rollback on degradation.

4) Incident review standards and postmortems
- Severity taxonomy: Sev0 (widespread outage), Sev1 (partial outage/customer impact), Sev2 (degraded), Sev3 (minor). Include impact definition and paging thresholds.
- Postmortem expectations: publish within 7 days of incident resolution. Must include timeline, impact, root cause(s), contributing factors, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates, and follow-up verification plan.
- Review: incidents that cross error budget red or are Sev0/Sev1 require SRE leadership review and presentation at monthly reliability review.

5) Operational tooling and dashboards
- Mandatory dashboards per service: SLO dashboard, availability/latency heatmap, capacity/queue metrics, error budget burn chart, top error types. Dashboards must be linked from the runbook.
- Alerting guidance: alerts should target actionable thresholds (e.g., queue length > 250 and p99 latency > 2s) and include runbook links and suggested first steps. Avoid noisy alerts; use multi-window checks where possible.
- Synthetic tests: 1-minute synthetic tests for critical flows, cross-region checks for routing and fallback verification.
- Tracing and logs: distributed traces must carry request_id and model_version tags. Log retention aligned with compliance (see security-and-compliance docs).

6) Runbook structure and minimum content
- Every runbook must include the following flat fields: title, owning team, on-call rotation link, primary contacts, symptoms, impact assessment, quick remediation steps (1-3), escalation steps, SLO link, dashboards, and post-incident follow-up checklist.
- Runbook template (text table):
  | Field | Example |
  |---|---|
  | Title | Generation API - high tail latency |
  | Owning team | eng-serving-runtime |
  | On-call | oncall-gen-api (PagerDuty) |
  | Symptoms | p95 latency > 500ms; backlog > 1000 requests |
  | Quick remediation | 1) Scale pool; 2) Enable degraded model fallback; 3) Clear request queue |
  | Escalation | Notify SRE lead, open incident, contact infra for capacity increase |
  | SLO link | /confluence/eng-sre/slo-generation-api |

7) Governance and review cadence
- Documentation must be reviewed at least annually or after any significant platform change.
- SRE onboarding: new services must have a vetted SLO and runbook before being marked production-ready.
- Exceptions: request via risk-and-exceptions with documented compensating controls.

Appendix: Quick checklists
- New service checklist: SLO defined, runbook created, dashboards in place, synthetic tests configured, incident review owner assigned.
- Pre-release checklist (major changes): run reliability test, estimate error budget impact, schedule canary rollout, notify SRE/infra.

Related pages and templates:
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks-index
- /confluence/eng-sre/slo-template
- /confluence/eng-sre/incident-postmortem-template

Contacts and ownership:
- Document owner: eng-sre (Ari Chen)
- Questions: eng-sre@redwood.example.com

This standard is intended to be prescriptive for teams that operate production inference services. Teams may adopt stricter thresholds for customer SLAs or regulated environments; any deviation must be documented and reviewed by eng-sre.
